newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian PM defends RBA gold sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Australian PM defends RBA gold sell-off.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard on Wednesday defended the Australian central bank's decision to sell a large slab of its gold reserves, insisting the move had not caused the precious metal's recent price dive.
Howard told reporters on Thursday Island, in Australia's far north, that gold producers themselves were more responsible for falling gold prices than the Reserve Bank of Australia's sale.

"If you look at the activities of gold mining companies, gold producers both in Australia and elsewhere, many of them have been themselves behaving in a way over recent weeks which has exerted a downward pressure on the price of gold," Howard said, without elaborating.

"The Reserve Bank of Australia took a sensible, prudent, completely unexceptionable and utterly defensible decision in the interests of Australia and in the interests of all of us in deciding to sell gold and put the proceeds into some interest-bearing securities."

The central bank said last Thursday it had sold 167 tonnes of gold over the past six months, about two thirds of its reserves. News of the sale contributed to a slump in the gold price to a 12-year low.
Industry groups have criticised the sale, saying it had helped drive gold prices down.
Australia is the world's third-biggest gold producer, but extraction costs are among the world's highest and the recent fall in gold prices means many mines are no longer viable.
